{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "# Usage: /ok-to-test [k8s-version]
# Examples:
# /ok-to-test
# /ok-to-test v1.18.4

name: e2e

on:
  issue_comment:
    types: [created]
  # Allows you to run this workflow manually from the Actions tab
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.head_ref || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  build:
    if: |
      contains(github.event.issue.html_url, '/pull/') &&
      startsWith(github.event.comment.body, '/ok-to-test') &&
      (github.event.comment.author_association == 'OWNER' || github.event.comment.author_association == 'MEMBER')
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@34e114876b0b11c390a56381ad16ebd13914f8d5 # v4.3.1
        with:
          ref: refs/pull/${{ github.event.issue.number }}/merge

      - name: Cache Go modules
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/go/pkg/mod
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-go-${{ hashFiles('go.mod', 'go.sum') }}

      - name: Set up QEMU
        id: qemu
        uses: docker/setup-qemu-action@c7c53464625b32c7a7e944ae62b3e17d2b600130 # v3.7.0
        with:
          cache-image: false

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@8d2750c68a42422c14e847fe6c8ac0403b4cbd6f # v3.12.0

      - name: Login to GitHub Container Registry
        uses: docker/login-action@4907a6ddec9925e35a0a9e82d7399ccc52663121 # v4.1.0
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: 1gtm
          password: ${{ secrets.LGTM_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Publish to GitHub Container Registry
        env:
          REGISTRY: ghcr.io/stashed
        run: |
          make release

      - name: Build
        env:
          REGISTRY: ghcr.io/appscodeci
        run: |
          make push

  config:
    if: |
      contains(github.event.issue.html_url, '/pull/') &&
      startsWith(github.event.comment.body, '/ok-to-test') &&
      (github.event.comment.author_association == 'OWNER' || github.event.comment.author_association == 'MEMBER')
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    needs: build
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.set-matrix.outputs.matrix }}
    steps:
      - id: set-matrix
        name: Generate test matrix
        env:
          COMMENT_BODY: ${{ github.event.comment.body }}
        run: |
          k8s=(v1.28.15 v1.34.0)

          IFS=' '
          read -ra COMMENT <<< "$COMMENT_BODY"
          if [ ! -z ${COMMENT[1]} ]; then
            k8s=(${COMMENT[1]})
          fi

          matrix=()
          for x in ${k8s[@]}; do
            matrix+=( $( jq -n -c --arg x "$x" '{"k8s":$x}' ) )
          done

          # https://stackoverflow.com/a/63046305/244009
          function join { local IFS="$1"; shift; echo "$*"; }
          matrix=$(echo "{"include":[$(join , ${matrix[@]})]}")
          echo $matrix
          echo "matrix=$matrix" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  kubernetes:
    name: Kubernetes
    needs: [build, config]
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    strategy:
      matrix: ${{ fromJson(needs.config.outputs.matrix) }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@34e114876b0b11c390a56381ad16ebd13914f8d5 # v4.3.1
        with:
          ref: refs/pull/${{ github.event.issue.number }}/merge

      - name: Cache Go modules
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/go/pkg/mod
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-go-${{ hashFiles('go.mod', 'go.sum') }}

      - name: Create Kubernetes ${{ matrix.k8s }} cluster
        id: kind
        uses: helm/kind-action@ef37e7f390d99f746eb8b610417061a60e82a6cc # v1.14.0
        with:
          version: v0.29.0
          config: hack/kubernetes/kind.yaml
          node_image: kindest/node:${{ matrix.k8s }}

      - name: Prepare cluster for testing
        id: local-path
        run: |
          echo "waiting for nodes to be ready ..."
          kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready nodes --all --timeout=5m
          kubectl get nodes
          echo
          kubectl version

      - name: Install NFS server dependencies
        run: |
          nodes=$(kubectl get nodes -o=jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{"\t"}{end}')
          for i in $nodes
          do
            echo "Installing NFS server dependencies in node: $i ...."
            docker exec $i apt-get update
            docker exec $i apt-get install -y nfs-kernel-server
          done

      - name: Check out installer
        run: |
          cd ..
          git clone https://github.com/stashed/installer.git
          cd installer
          git checkout master

      - name: Run e2e tests
        env:
          REGISTRY: ghcr.io/stashed
          REGISTRY_SECRET: regcred
          TEST_CREDENTIALS: ${{ secrets.TEST_CREDENTIALS }}
          GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON_KEY }}
        run: |
          echo "preparing test credentials"
          mkdir -p hack/config
          echo -n "$TEST_CREDENTIALS" > hack/config/.env
          echo >> hack/config/.env
          echo "GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON_KEY=$(echo $GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON_KEY)" >> hack/config/.env
          make install
          echo
          sleep 10
          make e2e-parallel",
  "rationale": "The workflow runs Go-based build and test steps in two sequential jobs (build and kubernetes) on ubuntu-24.04. Both jobs check out the same repository and execute `make` commands that download Go modules. The repository contains go.mod and go.sum (lockfile), satisfying the preconditions for P-LIT-GHA-CACHE. The experiment example (batch-interactive-three--f6d2974a5cef7cc9) demonstrates adding a `actions/cache@v4` step for `~/go/pkg/mod` keyed by runner OS and the hash of go.mod/go.sum, which reduced median elapsed time by ~6% in a measured CI workflow. No existing cache step is present. Adding the cache step in both jobs preserves all build/test coverage, requires no new permissions or network access, and aligns with the pattern's mechanism of dependency caching. The concurrency cancel-in-progress and matrix fail-fast (default true) are already configured, so no changes for P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE or P-LIT-FAIL-FAST are needed.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-interactive-three--f6d2974a5cef7cc9", "pattern:P-LIT-GHA-CACHE"]
}

The user wants me to analyze the provided workflow and evidence to propose a CI optimization. Let me first understand the workflow and the evidence.

The workflow is an e2e test workflow triggered by issue comments with "/ok-to-test". It has three jobs:
1. `build` - builds and pushes Docker images
2. `config` - generates a test matrix for Kubernetes versions
3. `kubernetes` - runs e2e tests on a Kind cluster with the matrix

The evidence includes several experiment examples and pattern catalogues. Let me look for relevant patterns that could apply to this workflow.

Looking at the patterns:
- P-LIT-GHA-CACHE: Cache dependency downloads (Go modules)
- P-LIT-FAIL-FAST: Cancel remaining matrix jobs after failure
- P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE: Cancel superseded runs (already has concurrency with cancel-in-progress)
- P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT: Bound jobs with custom timeout
- P-LIT-FAILED-JOB-FIRST: Run previously failing jobs first
- P-LIT-HISTORY-TIMEOUT: Derive timeout from history
- P-LIT-ENV-CACHE: Reuse validated build environments
- P-LIT-BAZEL-PARALLEL/INCREMENTAL/DEPS: Bazel-related (not applicable, this is Go/Make)
- P-LIT-GHA-CACHE has an experiment example showing caching Go modules

The workflow uses Go (go.mod, go.sum present) and has a build step that runs `make release` and `make push`. The kubernetes job runs `make install` and `make e2e-parallel`.

The build job doesn't seem to cache Go modules. The kubernetes job checks out code and runs make commands that likely download Go dependencies.

Let me check if there's a Go module cache opportunity. The workflow has:
- `actions/checkout` in both build and kubernetes jobs
- Build job runs `make release` and `make push`
- Kubernetes job runs `make install` and `make e2e-parallel`

The repository has go.mod and go.sum, so it's a Go project. The P-LIT-GHA-CACHE pattern suggests caching Go modules at `~/go/pkg/mod` with key based on go.mod and go.sum.

However, the build job uses Docker Buildx and pushes to GHCR. The kubernetes job runs on ubuntu-24.04 and uses Kind. The Go modules would be downloaded during `make install` and `make e2e-parallel`.

But wait - the build job runs `make release` and `make push` which might also download Go modules. However, the build job uses Docker, so it might be building inside containers.

Looking at the Makefile snippet, it shows `GO_PKG := stash.appscode.dev` and various Go-related variables. The `make release` and `make push` likely build Go binaries.

The kubernetes job runs `make install` and `make e2e-parallel` which would also need Go modules.

Since both jobs run on ubuntu-24.04 and checkout the code, they could benefit from Go module caching.

But there's a concurrency group that cancels in-progress runs. The workflow is triggered by issue comments on PRs.

Now, let me check the evidence for P-LIT-GHA-CACHE. There's an experiment example (batch-interactive-three--f6d2974a5cef7cc9) that shows adding a cache step for Go modules. The pattern catalogue also describes this.

The preconditions for P-LIT-GHA-CACHE are:
- Repeated dependency fetching is measurable
- Cache inputs include lockfile and environment

This repository has go.mod and go.sum (lockfile), and uses Go 1.25 (from go.mod). The workflow runs on ubuntu-24.04.

The contraindications are:
- Mutable or untrusted cached content
- An equivalent cache already exists

I don't see any existing cache in the workflow. So this could be applicable.

However, I need to consider: the build job uses Docker Buildx and might build in containers. The kubernetes job runs directly on the runner. The Go module cache would be most beneficial for the kubernetes job which runs `make install` and `make e2e-parallel` on the host.

But the build job also runs `make release` and `make push` on the host (before Docker). Let me check the build job steps:
1. Checkout
2. Set up QEMU
3. Set up Docker Buildx
4. Login to GHCR
5. Publish to GHCR (runs `make release`)
6. Build (runs `make push`)

So `make release` and `make push` run on the host, not in Docker. They would download Go modules.

The kubernetes job:
1. Checkout
2. Create Kind cluster
3. Prepare cluster
4. Install NFS server dependencies
5. Check out installer
6. Run e2e tests (runs `make install` and `make e2e-parallel`)

Both jobs download Go modules. Adding a Go module cache could speed up both.

But wait - the build job has `runs-on: ubuntu-24.04` and the kubernetes job also has `runs-on: ubuntu-24.04`. They run sequentially (kubernetes needs build). So the cache could be shared between them if they run on the same runner? But GitHub Actions doesn't guarantee same runner for different jobs. However, the cache is stored in GitHub's cache storage, so it can be restored across jobs and runs.

The cache key would be `${{ runner.os }}-go-${{ hashFiles('go.mod', 'go.sum') }}` which is the same for both jobs.

So adding a cache step in both jobs (or at least in the kubernetes job which runs longer) could help.

But the instruction says: "Preserve the intended build and test coverage, and avoid unrelated changes." And "Do not weaken permissions or add privileged actions, secrets, publishing/deployment operations or new network access."

Adding a cache action is a standard optimization.

Now, let me check if there are other applicable patterns.

P-LIT-FAIL-FAST: The kubernetes job uses a matrix strategy for Kubernetes versions (v1.28.15 and v1.34.0 by default). The matrix is generated dynamically. The strategy doesn't have `fail-fast` set (defaults to true). Actually, the default for `strategy.fail-fast` is true. So it already cancels other matrix jobs if one fails. The evidence shows changing from `fail-fast: false` to `fail-fast: true`. But here it's already true by default. So no change needed.

P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE: The workflow already has concurrency with `cancel-in-progress: true`. So this is already implemented.

P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT: The jobs don't have explicit timeouts. The workflow has a default timeout (6 hours). The kubernetes job could take a long time. But we don't have history to set a good timeout. The pattern requires "Representative successful-duration history exists". We don't have that data. So not applicable.

P-LIT-FAILED-JOB-FIRST: This is a CI service level feature, not workflow YAML. The pattern scope is "ci_service". Not applicable via workflow change.

P-LIT-HISTORY-TIMEOUT: Similar, needs history.

P-LIT-ENV-CACHE: Reuse validated build environments. This is more about caching the entire environment (like Docker images or VM snapshots). The pattern is from a paper about Travis-to-Kotinos migration. Might not be directly applicable to GitHub Actions.

P-LIT-GHA-CACHE seems the most applicable and has direct evidence from an experiment.

The experiment example shows:
- Adding a step: `- name: Cache Go modules` with `uses: actions/cache@v4` and path `~/go/pkg/mod`, key `${{ runner.os }}-go-${{ hashFiles('go.mod', 'go.sum') }}`

This should be added before the step that downloads dependencies (e.g., before `make release` in build job and before `make install` in kubernetes job).

But the build job runs `make release` and `make push`. The kubernetes job runs `make install` and `make e2e-parallel`. Both would benefit.

However, the build job also sets up Docker Buildx and QEMU. The cache step should be after checkout and before the first `make` command.

Let me structure the change:

In the `build` job, after checkout and before `make release`:
```yaml
      - name: Cache Go modules
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/go/pkg/mod
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-go-${{ hashFiles('go.mod', 'go.sum') }}
```

In the `kubernetes` job, after checkout and before `make install`:
```yaml
      - name: Cache Go modules
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/go/pkg/mod
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-go-${{ hashFiles('go.mod', 'go.sum') }}
```

But wait - the kubernetes job also checks out the installer repository (`git clone https://github.com/stashed/installer.git`). That might have its own go.mod. But the main project's go.mod is what matters for `make install` and `make e2e-parallel` which run in the main repo.

The cache key uses `hashFiles('go.mod', 'go.sum')` which are in the checked out repo. Since both jobs checkout the same ref (`refs/pull/${{ github.event.issue.number }}/merge`), the hash will be the same.

Now, I need to verify that the workflow doesn't already have caching. Looking at the original workflow, there's no cache step.

Also, the evidence IDs: I should use the experiment example document_id: `experiment:batch-interactive-three--f6d2974a5cef7cc9` and the pattern catalogue document_id: `pattern:P-LIT-GHA-CACHE`.

The instruction says: "Use only supported evidence IDs; APPLY requires at least one."

I'll include both.

Now, the decision: APPLY with the updated workflow.

Let me create the updated workflow YAML.

I need to be careful to preserve all existing steps and only add the cache steps.

Let me write the updated workflow.
